children: Hackers who broke into Japanese online brokerage Rakuten Securities earlier this month obtained asset balance details for about 1.68mn customers, including what they held in stocks and investment trusts,
reported on November 25. The firm said the balance data formed part of 4.41mn sets of personal information exposed in the attack.

The update widens the scope of a breach the company first disclosed earlier in November. The brokerage has now confirmed that seven more categories of data were taken beyond those named in its original report. These include bank deposit account details, gender and nationality.
Names, telephone numbers, home addresses and dates of birth were among the personal details compromised in the unauthorised access, according to the securities firm.

The stolen material also covered about 2.71mn sets of data on how much customers held in assets, along with roughly 14,000 records of their yearly income. The company said neither category contained precise figures. Both came from information customers had reported themselves or from income and asset ranges they had chosen to select when filling in forms.
A much larger group of customers was affected to a lesser degree. For about 11.98mn accounts, the leaked information was limited to customer codes and login IDs, the brokerage said.

title: Rakuten Securities breach in Japan exposes 4.41mn records
